papers.title: Daylight, Daily Rhythms, and Downstream Physiology: A Translational Study in Diurnal Nile Grass Rats (Arvicanthis niloticus).
papers.summary: This study compared circadian and physiological effects of different lighting conditions in diurnal Nile grass rats, finding that daylight-equivalent lighting produced stronger entrainment than fluorescent indoor light. Fluorescent light increased diabetic rate and reduced sperm motility, suggesting health consequences of circadian disruption.

papers.title: Cortical isolation separates rhythmic synchrony from network integration in the human neocortex.
papers.summary: The study compared cortical activity in humans across wakefulness, sleep, and isolated cortex slices, finding that isolating cortex increases gamma synchronization but reduces network integration and dimensionality. This suggests local circuits generate gamma while long-range inputs support diverse dynamics.

papers.title: REM sleep prefrontal high-frequency oscillation chains mediate distinct cortical - hippocampal reactivation patterns compared to NREM sleep.
papers.summary: This study in rodents identifies prefrontal cortical high-frequency oscillation (HFO) chains during REM sleep that phase-modulate with theta oscillations and coordinate sparse hippocampal-cortical reactivation of spatial memories, contrasting with NREM ripples. A cortical network model incorporating acetylcholine effects reproduces these distinct REM and NREM activity patterns, linking REM HFOs to memory consolidation.

papers.title: Circadian reprogramming of inflammation and metabolism in chronic kidney disease.
papers.summary: This study performed time-series RNA-seq on kidneys from CKD mice, showing disrupted circadian transcriptome with acquired rhythmicity in immune-inflammatory genes and decreased rhythmicity in metabolic genes. Dapagliflozin partially restored core clock gene rhythms and improved renal function.

papers.title: Quantitative EEG-Based Detection of Poststroke Delirium Endotypes and Their Association With Biomarkers of Inflammation.
papers.summary: This observational cohort study used quantitative EEG in stroke patients, finding that connectivity metrics detect poststroke delirium with high accuracy and correlate with inflammatory biomarkers. This suggests EEG connectivity captures delirium endotypes beyond clinical phenotype.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Affective Disorders Diagnosis: An Evaluation and Validation Study.
papers.summary: The study introduced 25 EEG features and evaluated their diagnostic utility for affective disorders using two resting-state datasets. It identified biomarkers with strong discriminative power and discussed challenges in EEG-based diagnosis and multimodal integration.

papers.title: Brain-wide reconfiguration of burst firing by psilocybin reveals 5-HT2A-dependent circuit dynamics
papers.summary: Using multi-region Neuropixels recordings in mice, this study found that psilocybin selectively reconfigured burst firing rather than mean firing rates across cortical, thalamic, and hippocampal circuits, with decreased hippocampal burst firing and bidirectional modulation in the thalamus. Most burst effects were abolished by the 5-HT2A antagonist ketanserin, indicating a 5-HT2A-dependent reconfiguration of burst coding underlying the psychedelic state.

papers.title: Time-of-day variation in endurance and strength performance, and physiological state across the waking day.
papers.summary: In a randomized crossover study of 15 healthy adults, short-duration cycling performance and handgrip strength peaked in the late afternoon/early evening (around 18:00), with significant time-of-day variation across the waking day. Physiological states, including tympanic temperature, sleepiness, blood glucose, and lactate, also varied diurnally, indicating time-of-day as a relevant factor in exercise testing.

papers.title: Functional network reorganization and thalamocortical gating as neurobiological markers of recovery in somatic symptom disorder: A 6-month longitudinal source EEG study.
papers.summary: This 6-month longitudinal source EEG study in 83 patients with somatic symptom disorder (SSD) and 80 controls found persistent reduction in gamma-band global efficiency in SSD, while clinical improvement was associated with reorganization of nodal efficiency in the left central sensorimotor region and longitudinal changes in thalamic spectral power. These findings suggest multilayered neurobiological changes underlie SSD recovery.

papers.title: Relationship between genetic risk, social jetlag, and obesity traits in a Turkish adult population.
papers.summary: In 223 Turkish adults, social jetlag was associated with higher BMI, but this association was attenuated after adjusting for a genetic risk score based on FTO, MC4R, and TCF7L2, and those with more risk alleles had higher BMI. Among participants with social jetlag, metabolic genetic risk was positively correlated with BMI and body fat measures, suggesting an interaction between circadian misalignment and genetic obesity susceptibility.

papers.title: Resting-State Functional Connectivity Alterations in Insomnia Disorder: A Systematic Review of Studies Published from 2020 to July 2025.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) studies in insomnia disorder published from 2020 to July 2025. It found alterations in multiple brain networks and sleep-wake hubs compatible with hyperarousal, but methodological heterogeneity precluded quantitative pooling, and cross-sectional designs limit causal inference.

papers.title: Reduced EEG Complexity and Its Association with Social Communication in Adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Multiscale Entropy Study
papers.summary: This EEG study in adults with autism spectrum disorder (ASD, n=47) and typically developing controls (n=40) found reduced multiscale entropy (MSE) at longer time scales in ASD across rest and movie-viewing conditions, which was associated with higher social affect scores on the ADOS-2. Event-related analyses showed attenuated differentiation of MSE between social and non-social movie windows in ASD, indicating reduced neural complexity relevant to social processing.

papers.title: DRP-1 and circadian rhythms: deciphering their impact on PCOS.
papers.summary: This review explores the role of Dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP-1) in mitochondrial fission and its potential link between circadian rhythm disruption and polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), particularly involving oxidative stress and hormonal imbalances. It highlights DRP-1 as a possible therapeutic target for addressing mitochondrial and circadian dysfunction in PCOS.

papers.title: DISE and Rhinomanometry Correlates of Response to Head-of-Bed Elevation in Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.summary: This study assessed associations between drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) findings and rhinomanometric parameters with response to 30° head-of-bed elevation (HOBE) in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) patients. HOBE significantly reduced AHI, with epiglottic and tongue base collapse scores strongly correlated with improvement, suggesting DISE may help characterize positional responsivity, though results are hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: Stage-Specific Effects of Maternal Circadian Rhythm Disruption during Pre-Pregnancy, Pregnancy, and Lactation on Behavioral and Neurobiological Outcomes in Male Rat Offspring.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of maternal circadian rhythm disruption during distinct reproductive stages (pre-pregnancy, pregnancy, lactation) on male rat offspring. Offspring from pre-pregnancy and pregnancy disruption showed increased anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors, altered hippocampal CA1 morphology, and molecular changes, while lactation disruption had fewer effects, suggesting stage-specific impacts on neurodevelopment.

papers.title: The eating habits and lifestyle habits of shift workers: findings from the 2018 National Health and Nutrition Survey, Japan.
papers.summary: This study compared eating habits and lifestyle characteristics between shift and daytime workers using data from the 2018 Japan National Health and Nutrition Survey (n=1,814). Both male and female shift workers consumed significantly less fish and shellfish and had shorter sleep duration, while female shift workers also consumed less milk and dairy products, suggesting targeted dietary and lifestyle adjustments for shift workers.

papers.title: Effect of obesity on pharmacokinetics and drug dosing of remimazolam in patients with obstructive sleep apnoea.
papers.summary: This study characterized remimazolam pharmacokinetics in volunteers with different obesity levels and obstructive sleep apnea severity using a population pharmacokinetic model. Total body weight significantly affected clearance and metabolite volume, but obstructive sleep apnea severity did not; the study recommends lean/ideal body weight for induction and adjusted body weight for maintenance in class 2/3 obesity.

papers.title: Circadian and behavioral timing in MASLD: a systematic review of human observational studies.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 24 human observational studies found that shift work showed the most consistent associations with MASLD, while chronotype, sleep timing, and other circadian exposures had less consistent or limited evidence. Heterogeneity and confounding preclude causal conclusions, and prospective studies with objective circadian phenotyping are needed.

papers.title: Exploring the Benefit of an OT-Led Modified CBT-I Sleep Intervention for Montana Veterans: A Pilot Study.
papers.journal: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
papers.summary: This pilot study tested a 5-week occupational therapy-led modified cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) program for Montana veterans with self-reported sleep disturbances. Participants showed improvements in sleep, occupational performance, and mental health, with high feasibility and acceptability, suggesting OT-led CBT-I may be effective in community settings.

papers.title: Utility of Cephalometry and Acoustic Pharyngometry for the Assessment of Moderate to Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea Before Treatment in Childhood.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 205 children with moderate-to-severe OSA found that cephalometric indices (FMA and hyoid bone distance) were independently associated with OAHI, but with weak explanatory power. Acoustic pharyngometry measures correlated with height and FMIA, indicating cephalometry provides additional endotypic information.

papers.title: Microstructural Brain Reserve Moderates the Associations Between 24-h Movement Behaviors and Cognition in Older Adults: Cross-Sectional Findings From the AGUEDA Trial.
papers.journal: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports
papers.summary: Cross-sectional analysis from the AGUEDA trial found no direct associations between 24-hour movement behaviors and cognition in older adults, but gray matter mean diffusivity (GMMD) moderated associations, particularly for episodic memory and light physical activity, indicating the importance of microstructural brain integrity.

papers.title: A U-shaped relationship between perceived chronic stress and the approach motivation: evidence from resting-state EEG.
papers.summary: In 60 undergraduates, perceived chronic stress showed a U-shaped relationship with resting-state EEG measures of approach motivation, including alpha frontal asymmetry and delta/theta power. This nonlinear pattern suggests that both low and high stress enhance baseline approach motivation, while moderate stress reduces it.

papers.title: Early-life GABA-A receptor blockade with bicuculline attenuates anxiety-like behaviors and cognitive deficits induced by 24-hr sleep deprivation in adult male rats.
papers.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
papers.summary: This study in male rats found that early-life transient blockade of GABA-A receptors with bicuculline prevented cognitive deficits and anxiety-like behaviors induced by 24-hr sleep deprivation in adulthood, and restored hippocampal antioxidant enzyme activities and MDA levels. This suggests a developmental role of early GABAergic signaling in resilience to sleep loss.

papers.title: Heart Rate Variability During Short-Term Electroencephalography.
papers.summary: The study measured heart rate variability (HRV) in 103 patients undergoing routine short-term EEG and found reduced HRV compared to normal values, indicating that a normal EEG does not predict normal HRV. HRV was stable across wakefulness and sleep stages, suggesting that measuring HRV during the first five minutes of EEG could provide useful prognostic information.

papers.title: Application of numerical simulation of upper airway flow field in pediatric obstructive sleep apnea with adenoid hypertrophy.
papers.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
papers.summary: Computational fluid dynamics simulations of the upper airway in children with adenoid hypertrophy showed that AH significantly reduced nasopharyngeal cross-sectional area, increasing pressure, flow velocity, and wall shear stress, while adenoidectomy restored airflow parameters to near-normal levels.

papers.title: Preoperative Resting-State EEG Features Associated With Chronic Postoperative Pain After Breast Cancer Surgery: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of breast cancer surgery patients, higher preoperative resting-state frontal gamma power and connectivity were associated with clinically significant chronic postoperative pain at 3 months. The study suggests frontal gamma activity may reflect baseline neurophysiological vulnerability to chronic pain.

papers.title: BDNF as a biomarker for insomnia in hemodialysis patients: influence of hypnotic medication use.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of hemodialysis patients found that higher plasma BDNF levels were associated with poor sleep quality only in those not using hypnotic medications, and BDNF levels were positively correlated with hypnotic medication use. The authors suggest BDNF may be a biomarker for insomnia in hemodialysis patients not taking hypnotics.

papers.title: Twenty-Four-Hour Movement Guidelines Adherence and Academic Performance From Childhood to Adolescence.
papers.journal: Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education
papers.summary: Using longitudinal data from 3973 Australian children, this study found that each additional wave of adherence to 24-hour movement guidelines (ages 6-13) was associated with higher Year 9 numeracy and reading scores. Adherence at exposure wave was linked to subsequent reading performance.

papers.title: Epilepsy Is Part of the CNS Phenotype in Classic Infantile Pompe Disease.
authors: Johanna M P Van Den Hout
papers.summary: This international retrospective study of 17 patients with classic infantile Pompe disease found that epilepsy is part of the CNS phenotype, with seizures occurring predominantly after age 7 years. Most patients had EEG abnormalities, cognitive impairment, white matter changes, and elevated serum neurofilament light chain, and 70% became seizure-free on antiseizure medication.

papers.title: Alamandine Attenuates Hypoxia-Induced Atrial Fibrillation in Rats: Involvement of Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress and Pyroptosis Pathways.
papers.summary: This study examined the effect of alamandine on atrial fibrillation induced by chronic intermittent hypoxia in rats. Alamandine reduced atrial fibrillation susceptibility and attenuated endoplasmic reticulum stress and pyroptosis-related protein expression, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic agent for AF.

papers.title: The Circadian Skin: Chronobiology as a New Frontier in Dermatological Therapy.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes evidence that skin has intrinsic circadian clocks regulating physiology and disease processes, and highlights chronodermatology as a promising approach. However, it notes most therapeutic applications require more prospective human trials before clinical recommendation.

papers.title: Wearable Sensors Offer Opportunities for Phenotyping Perinatal Mood Disorders: a Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review discusses how wearable sensors can monitor sleep, circadian rhythms, and hormonal changes to phenotype perinatal mood disorders, potentially enabling earlier diagnosis and personalized interventions. It highlights the need for continuous monitoring to differentiate risk and improve maternal well-being.

papers.title: Mapping the Evidence for Operator Syndrome Among Special Operations Forces: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review systematically mapped the evidence for 'Operator Syndrome' in Special Operations Forces, identifying six sources. It found the construct is conceptually heterogeneous with no consensus definition, limited empirical support, and substantial overlap with other conditions such as mild traumatic brain injury and PTSD.

papers.title: A high-rate 480-target hybrid BCI system based on SSVEP and sEMG.
papers.summary: This paper presents a hybrid brain-computer interface combining steady-state visual evoked potentials and surface electromyography to encode 480 targets. In online experiments, it achieved an average classification accuracy of 84.55% and an information transfer rate of 260.07 bits/min, demonstrating high performance for large command sets.

papers.title: Maladaptive coping strategies mediate the relationship between perceived differential treatment and sleep health among women.
papers.summary: This study analyzed data from 31,443 women in the Sister Study and found that maladaptive coping strategies mediated the relationship between perceived differential treatment based on race-ethnicity and poor sleep quality and insomnia symptoms, particularly among non-Hispanic Black and White women. The findings suggest that addressing maladaptive coping may reduce sleep disturbances.

papers.title: Linking disease severity and mortality in obstructive sleep apnea: the role of the endothelial activation and stress index.
papers.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: This study analyzed NHANES data (n=9,797) and a clinical dataset (n=258) to show that higher EASIX levels are associated with increased all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in OSA, and significantly correlated with OSA severity indices (AHI, ODI). Machine learning models highlighted EASIX as a key predictor, suggesting its potential as a biomarker for risk stratification.

papers.title: Expanding the Clinical Spectrum of DHX30-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: A Case Report and a Scoping Review.
papers.journal: Journal of intellectual disability research : JIDR
papers.summary: This paper presents a case of a patient with global developmental delay and microtia carrying a de novo pathogenic DHX30 missense variant, along with a scoping review of 51 individuals with DHX30-related neurodevelopmental disorder. The review confirms common features such as motor delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and feeding difficulties, and suggests that microtia may be a novel manifestation.

papers.title: Nutritional Strategies for Recovery in Overhead Athletes: A Review.
papers.journal: HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery
papers.summary: This review discusses nutritional strategies to optimize recovery in overhead athletes after intense exercise, focusing on replenishing glycogen, repairing muscle, rehydrating, and addressing inflammation and sleep. It provides guidance on carbohydrate and fluid intake, protein synthesis, and meal timing to support recovery and immune function.

papers.title: Predictors of Paid Employment Status Among Individuals With Spinal Cord Injury in South Korea: An Exploratory Study Using Random Forest Analysis.
papers.summary: Using random forest analysis on survey data from 538 individuals with spinal cord injury in South Korea, this study identified predictors of paid employment, including higher household income, younger age, higher self-efficacy, better quality of life, access to vocational rehabilitation, and absence of disability benefits. These findings can inform policies to improve employment opportunities.

papers.title: Beyond Ergonomics Training: Added Effects of a Supervised, Equipment-Free Workplace Exercise Program on Musculoskeletal Symptoms, Sleep, and Burnout in Artisanal Pastry Workers: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial with 60 male börek workers found that adding a 12-week supervised, equipment-free exercise program to ergonomics education significantly reduced musculoskeletal symptoms compared to education alone, with improvements also in sleep and burnout. The study calls for objective confirmation due to self-reported outcomes.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
